correctness.rationale: Independent complements have only the two structural forms proved in RESULT.md. The one-side form needs at least two selected vertices on that side, and two suffice; the two-side form is exactly one deleted matching pair and has size \(2n-2\). This proves \(\min\{n+2,2n-2\}\) and all equality cases, with exhaustive finite corroboration.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are the canonical perfect-matching deletion of balanced complete bipartite graphs. The theorem sharpens the known complete-bipartite benchmark into an exact perturbation result, classifies all optimal configurations, and isolates a nontrivial boundary transition at \(n=4\).
